summary: In this excerpt from a fiction novel (Book 6, part 170), Russell recalls Arthur's remark that Russell asked for help only out of convenience, and Arthur reports that Sonya Halliday secured a deal with the Feds, with Agent Jones agreeing to make the matter go away. Arthur tells Russell that Dr. Martinez is hospitalized with symptoms including hallucinations and personality changes, raising doubt over whether the proof she supposedly wrote was real. Russell is shaken, feeling his life damaged, and considers whether to visit Martinez.
one_line: Russell learns from Arthur that Halliday secured a deal with the Feds, and that Martinez may have been hallucinating when she claimed her proof.
key_facts: Arthur tells Russell that Russell's past requests for help were out of convenience, not because Russell needed help.
Arthur says "We'll make a real person out of you yet."
Arthur credits Sonya for getting things squared with the Feds, saying she kept her cool and held her ground.
Sonya told the Feds they had to leave Russell be, and Agent Jones said she would make it all go away.
Russell wonders whether Halliday defended him because she still wanted him to work with her on advancements to her field.
Martinez's condition is described as not hopeful, with symptoms including hallucinations and personality changes.
Martinez's associates say she might have been thinking things that are not real.
Russell considers that the proof Martinez wrote might have been nothing but nonsense.
Russell says, "You don't think she ever had the proof," and Arthur replies, "Don't know. Likely we'll never know."
Russell feels the room become too close and pushes himself up, his equilibrium wobbling before he finds his balance.
Arthur tells Russell that Dr. Martinez can be visited because they are letting them.
Russell asks, "What's the point?" and suggests the visit might be to say goodbye.
Russell tells Arthur, "I didn't know her that well," and thinks Martinez destroyed him.
